propositions: CPython 3.12+ warns when fork() runs in a multithreaded host; Python 3.14 will no longer default to fork, causing grounding harness lifecycle tests to fail or emit warnings
The grounding harness hard-codes POSIX fork context, which allows unpicklable closures to work but violates the serialization contract and hides thread-safety issues

Worker callables, arguments, and results must be pickleable and importable at module level under spawn context; non-pickleable inputs and receive unpickling failures should return abstaining RunResult without raising
Switching default context from fork to spawn preserves 46 of 47 existing lifecycle tests; the one failure is a spawn-incompatible fixture that attaches an unpicklable local closure
Callers must explicitly opt into fork context, accepting responsibility for thread-safety; the public API contract and escape hatch must be documented
